children.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records
detail.summary: Objective records in quantum systems emerge when information is redundantly encoded in the environment, allowing multiple independent observers to access the same state without perturbing it. This process relies on decoherence to suppress interference terms, thereby stabilizing pointer states. The transition to classicality is not just a loss of coherence but an active proliferation of information, a prerequisite for the public reliability of physical records.
detail.reason: Synthesized recent findings on quantum-to-classical transitions and informational redundancy.
